'''Graham F. Hatfull''' is the Eberly Family Professor of Biotechnology at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he studies [[bacteriophage]]s.<ref name="pitt">{{cite web |title=Graham Hatfull {{!}} Department of Biological Sciences {{!}} University of Pittsburgh |url=https://www.biology.pitt.edu/person/graham-hatfull |website=www.biology.pitt.edu |access-date=8 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He has been an [[HHMI]] professor since 2002, and is the creator of their [[SEA-PHAGES]] program.<ref name="hhmidev">{{cite web |title=HHMI Professors {{!}} HHMI.org |url=https://www.hhmi.org/developing-scientists/hhmi-professors#Overview |website=www.hhmi.org |access-date=8 May 2019 |archive-date=22 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122052116/https://www.hhmi.org/developing-scientists/hhmi-professors#Overview |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2024, he was elected as a permanent member of the National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 NAS Election |url=https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430193331/https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |website=National Academy of Science Website |access-date=1 May 2024}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Hatfull studied biological sciences at [[Westfield College]], [[University of London]] from 1975 to 1978.<ref name="lab">{{cite web |title=Graham Hatfull |url=http://www.hatfull.org/graham-hatfull |website=Hatfull Lab |access-date=8 May 2019}}</ref> He received his PhD from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1981.<ref name=pitt/> He did postdoctoral research at [[Yale University]] and the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]].<ref name=lab/>

In 2002,<ref name="asm">{{cite journal |last1=Hatfull |first1=Graham F. |title=Innovations in Undergraduate Science Education: Going Viral |issue=16 |journal=Journal of Virology |volume=89 |pages=8111–8113 |language=en |doi=10.1128/JVI.03003-14 |pmid=26018168 |pmc=4524241 |date=15 August 2015}}</ref> he developed the [[SEA-PHAGES]], originally the PHIRE (Phage Hunters Integrating Research and Education) program,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Temple |first1=Louise |last2=Lewis |first2=Lynn |title=Phage on the stage |journal=Bacteriophage |volume=5 |issue=3 |article-number=e1062589 |doi=10.1080/21597081.2015.1062589 |pmid=26442195 |pmc=4588534 |date=22 June 2015}}</ref> which he originally developed to include 10-12 students per year.<ref name=hhmidev/> The program existed only at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] from 2002 to 2008, when the HHMI created the Science Education Alliance Phage Hunters Advancing Genomics and Evolutionary Science (SEA-PHAGES) program. The first year of SEA-PHAGES, the program had 12 participative universities. The program has since spread to more than 100 universities and thousands of students per year,<ref name=hhmidev/><ref>{{cite web |title=Science Education Alliance {{!}} HHMI.org |url=https://www.hhmi.org/developing-scientists/science-education-alliance |website=www.hhmi.org |access-date=8 May 2019}}</ref> with more than 50,000 total students having participated by 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=Sarah C. P. |date=2025-11-19 |title=QnAs with Graham F. Hatfull |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q137003933 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=122 |issue=47 |doi=10.1073/PNAS.2530455122|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Much of Hatfull's research focuses on understanding and characterizing [[Bacteriophage|bacteriophages]], which has led to using [[Phage therapy|phage therapies]] to treat ''[[Mycobacterium]]'' infections in some patients.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors ==
Hatfull is a member of the [[American Academy of Microbiology]], a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and in 2020 became a member of the [[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2020|title=New Members}}</ref>

He is also the winner of the 2013 Carski Foundation Distinguished Undergraduate Teaching Award <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/six-aaas-members-win-american-society-microbiology-award|title = Six AAAS Members Win American Society for Microbiology Award &#124; American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref> and the 2020 Peter Wildy Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://microbiologysociety.org/news/society-news/prize-lecture-winners-2020.html|title=Prize Lecture winners 2020}}</ref>

In 2024, Hatfull was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 NAS Election |url=https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430193331/https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2024-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2024 |website=National Academy of Science Website |access-date=1 May 2024}}</ref> According to the Academy "[members] are elected to the National Academy of Sciences in recognition of their distinguished and continuing achievements in original research. Membership is a widely accepted mark of excellence in science and is considered one of the highest honors that a scientist can receive. Current NAS membership totals approximately 2,400 members and 500 international members, of which approximately 190 have received Nobel prizes."<ref>{{cite web |title=National Academy Membership Overview |url=https://www.nasonline.org/membership/ |website=National Academy of Science Webpage |access-date=1 May 2024}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
